findings.title: Engine report surface has no tenant dimension; any signed-in org can list, run and download every org's engine reports
findings.description: The cloud routes authenticate the session for organizationId but never use it for scoping; EngineClient has no tenant parameter and one shared token; the engine host keeps a single global markting-reports.json index and serves any artefact to any valid token. Org A's runs (requested_by, windows, platform summaries, files) appear on org B's Reports page and B can download A's HTML/PDF. A global asyncio.Lock serialises all runs while the cloud allows 120 runs/min per org, so one tenant can starve others. Mitigating: the host refuses to boot unless data mode is 'sample', so today the leaked content is synthetic.
findings.recommendation: Store report runs in adport Postgres keyed by organization_id and serve only own rows (or run one engine per tenant / pass an org-scoped caller_ref and partition the engine index and artefact dir per caller). Lower the per-org report rate limit and queue runs instead of a global lock.

findings.title: Assistant is one synchronous HTTP request that may run for minutes; no streaming, no job, no persisted messages
findings.description: maxDuration=300 only informs deployment platforms and does nothing on the standalone Node server; the engine call blocks for up to 240 s (max 900 s) behind any proxy/LB that terminates idle responses. Conversation state lives only in React state; a reload loses it and threadId; listThreads is unused so markting_threads records ownership only. Each in-flight turn pins a request and a DB pool slot.
findings.recommendation: Make engine turns asynchronous (enqueue + poll or SSE stream), persist messages per thread, add cancel, put threadId in the URL for resumption.

findings.title: Bridge throws outside its try/catch when the translated tool is not registered; proposal left dangling on the engine with no record or hand-off

findings.title: Apply is not atomic across concurrent approvers; dashboard scans pending rows O(n) with a hard 200 cap
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/repository.ts (PostgresPendingStore.get/delete, no FOR UPDATE or conditional consume)
findings.description: Two admins or two tabs clicking Apply within the provider round-trip both pass get(), both call applyWrite, both write an 'applied' audit event. Only idempotent budget/status updates are translated so the platform effect is benign today, but the audit double-counts and a non-idempotent tool would double-apply. listPendingOperations(...,200).find returns 404 for rows beyond 200. markPendingOutcome runs only after success so provenance can stay 'pending' on a consumed row. Upstream engine weakness, newly exposed by a second human-driven surface.
findings.recommendation: Consume first with update ... set consumed_at=now() where id=$1 and consumed_at is null returning * (compensate on provider failure) or select ... for update skip locked; fetch by id; write provenance in the same transaction.

findings.title: Defence-in-depth gaps: unsafe-inline scripts, non-HttpOnly auth cookies, no Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site check on cookie-authenticated JSON POSTs

findings.title: jsonb columns asserted into TS types, never parsed (except policy and sandbox state)

findings.title: Four parallel error hierarchies glued by string matching; AdportError codes stretched semantically

POLICY_VIOLATION details include the whole org policy, serialized to MCP callers via toJSON(). No security impact found (REST returns message only; MCP caller is the tenant's own agent).
findings.recommendation: Typed AuthenticationError mapped centrally in apiError; a cloud-side error union (UNAUTHENTICATED/FORBIDDEN/NOT_FOUND/CONFLICT/UPSTREAM) instead of overloading core codes; redact `policy` from error details.

findings.title: PolicyEngine.apply has no atomic claim: concurrent applies of one pending id execute the provider write twice
evidence: node d7-double-apply.mjs => exit 0: 'S1 concurrent apply: applyWrite calls = 2 | outcomes = fulfilled, fulfilled | applied audit events = 2'
findings.description: apply() reads the pending row, calls provider.applyWrite, then soft-deletes. The store contract (delete(): void) cannot express a claim and the Postgres delete has no 'consumed_at is null' guard or returning, so every concurrent caller that passes get() executes. For create-kind tools (10 provider packages) this is a duplicate campaign with real spend; for update-kind tools the audit log double-counts.
findings.recommendation: Add claim(id) to PendingOperationStore implemented as a conditional 'update ... where consumed_at is null and expires_at > now() returning *' and call it before applyWrite; or wrap the apply route in a transaction with select ... for update. Add a concurrency test to packages/core.

findings.title: Apply has no atomic consume and no idempotency: concurrent or retried Apply can execute the provider write twice
findings.description: PolicyEngine.apply does pending.get (no lock) -> provider.applyWrite -> audit.append -> pending.delete, where delete is an unconditional soft-consume update with no consumed_at-is-null guard or returning. The route wraps nothing in a transaction and markPendingOutcome runs afterwards. Two concurrent applies (two tabs, two admins, retry after gateway timeout) or a crash between applyWrite and delete yield a second provider write and a mismatched audit trail. Only a client-side busy flag guards against double submission.
findings.recommendation: Make consumption the first durable step (update ... where id=$1 and consumed_at is null returning *) in a transaction that also writes an approval.apply_requested outbox row; perform the provider write with the pending id as idempotency key where supported; record approval.applied or approval.apply_failed explicitly. Add a claim() primitive to PendingOperationStore upstream.

findings.title: Chat turns are end-to-end synchronous with no cancellation or idempotency; client timeout orphans engine work and invites duplicate turns

findings.recommendation: Make a turn a job: insert assistant_turns row + turn.requested event, return 202, worker calls the engine with a dedupe key the markting host honours via DedupeStore, emits turn.completed/failed; UI polls or subscribes. Engine already has astream plumbing for progress.

findings.title: Stale awaiting_approval proposals are re-bridged on later unrelated turns; unsupported proposals are never handed back to the engine
evidence: probe_async.py: turn2 on same thread returned turn1 proposal b3f6cff2 awaiting_approval with interrupted=false
findings.description: The bridge previews whenever proposal.state === 'awaiting_approval' regardless of interrupted or turn; the engine returns the newest proposal on the thread. The unsupported branch never calls handoff, and handoff failures are swallowed, so the engine proposal stays awaiting_approval and every later turn in the thread re-translates it: repeated unsupported cards, or for supported proposals a second pending_operations row and validated audit event with the provenance upsert overwriting pending_operation_id (orphaning the first).
findings.recommendation: Bridge only proposals created in this turn (or require interrupted===true), always hand off unsupported proposals, persist hand-off as its own retried step (handoff_pending/handed_off/handoff_failed) and emit engine.handoff_failed instead of swallowing.

findings.title: Refresh-token rotation is performed inline during reads; a persistence failure loses a rotated token

The client instance is request-scoped, so a transient DB failure fails the read and discards the only copy of the new refresh token, killing the connection until re-authorization. The CAS logic itself is tested and correct.
findings.recommendation: Persist with bounded retry before returning from refresh, emit credential.rotated/rotation_failed events, and consider a near-expiry rotation job rather than rotating only inside reads.

key_findings: Every user-facing long operation (chat turn, report run, apply, webhook, deletion) is synchronous inside an HTTP request; no outbox, queue, worker or application scheduler exists (only pg_cron SQL jobs).

Approval apply has no atomic claim or idempotency key: concurrent or retried Apply, or a crash between provider write and consume, can execute the ad-platform write twice (P1, upstream PolicyEngine + PostgresPendingStore).

Report runs are serialized by one in-process asyncio.Lock shared by all tenants and the sync compute/WeasyPrint render blocks the engine event loop (measured 1.36s stall per 1.42s run); the report index is global so every org sees every run (P1).

The engine->adport hand-off is a best-effort saga: unsupported proposals are never handed back and hand-off errors are swallowed, so the engine returns the stale awaiting_approval proposal on the next unrelated turn and the bridge re-previews it (verified at runtime).
Chat turns have a 240s client abort with no cancellation or idempotency on the engine side; the monthly report deterministically fails on the demo fixture with a 500.

Stripe webhook dedupe is read-then-write outside the transaction with no event ordering guard; token rotation happens inline in reads and a DB failure discards the only copy of a rotated refresh token.

No event exists for preview expiry or outcome measurement; audit_events (15-value CHECK enum) is the only event stream and cannot grow without migrations; retention misses markting_*, engine and MCP OAuth tables.

Recommended design: domain_events outbox written transactionally in Supabase + SKIP LOCKED worker as a compose service, pg_cron as the tick (expiry, cadence, batched retention), Supabase Realtime for UI push; external broker deferred.

findings.title: No resource-owner/admin revocation of MCP OAuth grants
findings.description: MCP grants are listed in the dashboard (listMcpOAuthGrants) but there is no authenticated endpoint for an owner/admin to revoke them. The only revocation path is RFC7009 POST /oauth/revoke, reachable only by the client presenting its own token.
findings.recommendation: Add an authenticated owner/admin revoke endpoint that sets revoked_at on all refresh+access tokens for a (client_id,user_id,resource) grant, wired to the existing grant listing.

findings.title: Refresh-token rotation lacks reuse detection / family revocation
findings.description: A consumed refresh token is accepted within a 60s grace and rejected afterwards, but reuse never revokes the token family (RFC 9700 §4.14.2). Theft is neither detected nor contained.
findings.recommendation: On reuse of a consumed refresh token outside the grace window, revoke all refresh+access tokens for the grant and log a security event instead of only rejecting the request.

findings.title: Token revocation does not cascade between access and refresh tokens
findings.description: Revoking a refresh token updates only the refresh table; revoking an access token updates only the access table. RFC 7009 §2.1 expects revoking a refresh token to invalidate derived access tokens; neither direction cascades, leaving up to 1h of valid access after a revoke.
findings.recommendation: When revoking a refresh token, also revoke access tokens for the same (client_id,user_id,resource).

findings.title: Consent endpoint relies on cookie SameSite, no explicit anti-CSRF token
findings.description: The consent POST mints an authorization code bound to sessionPrincipal() with no CSRF/nonce. Protection depends on the Supabase session cookie's SameSite (Lax default, not overridden in code; unverifiable at runtime). With open DCR, if cookies were ever SameSite=None a cross-site auto-submit could silently issue a code to an attacker-registered redirect URI.
findings.recommendation: Embed a per-session signed CSRF token in the consent form and verify on POST; pin cookie sameSite explicitly in code.

findings.title: Bounded 60s refresh-token replay window (documented tradeoff)
findings.description: A consumed refresh token is intentionally honored for 60s to tolerate concurrent scheduled clients, each acceptance minting a fresh pair. Low risk but a real replay window that compounds the missing reuse detection in E2-02.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable once E2-02 lands; consider narrowing the grace or scoping it to a client fingerprint.

findings.title: Open unauthenticated dynamic client registration
findings.description: DCR is open (per MCP spec), rate-limited 20 per 60s per forwarded IP, with sound redirect-URI validation. Not a defect alone but amplifies E2-01/E2-04 blast radius.
findings.recommendation: Keep per spec but ensure E2-01 ships; consider a global registration cap and pruning of unused clients.

key_findings: Hosted broker is strong: state is single-use, SHA-256-hashed at rest, user+org bound, 10m TTL, consumed atomically under FOR UPDATE; PKCE S256 for Google/Microsoft; redirect URIs pinned to env base URL (never the Host header); verifiers AES-256-GCM encrypted with per-tenant AAD.

MCP OAuth 2.1 core is solid: PKCE S256 enforced with challenge-format check, single-use auth codes with client/redirect/resource binding, RFC 8707 audience binding, HS256 JWT with alg+kid+typ pinned and DB-backed jti/claim cross-check, RFC 9728 WWW-Authenticate pointer.

P1: no resource-owner/admin way to revoke an MCP grant — dashboard lists grants but only the token-holding client can revoke, so a rogue/compromised MCP client cannot be disconnected for up to 30 days.
P2: refresh-token rotation has no reuse detection or token-family revocation (RFC 9700), enabling silent refresh-token-theft takeover.
P2: revocation does not cascade — revoking a refresh token leaves derived access tokens valid up to 1h (RFC 7009).
P3: consent endpoint has no explicit CSRF token and depends on the (inferred Lax) Supabase cookie SameSite; combined with open DCR this is a latent consent-CSRF path if cookie policy changes.
82 OAuth unit tests pass; redirect manipulation, code replay, and token substitution attempts were all correctly rejected by the code paths reviewed.

However the MCP refresh-rotation framing implies standard rotation security while the code omits the reuse-detection/family-revocation RFC 9700 expects (E2-02), and listMcpOAuthGrants presents grants as tenant-visible credential metadata (mcp-oauth-repository.ts:45-49) yet the product offers no revocation action a user would expect from such a list (E2-01). No code was found to contradict a documented security claim outright.
E2.not_verified: Runtime SameSite attribute of the Supabase session cookie (inferred Lax default; E2-04 severity depends on it). The DB-backed behaviors in test/mcp-oauth.database.test.ts (rotation grace, post-grace rejection, access-token revoke) were read as DOCUMENTED, not executed, because no Postgres is available in the sandbox — only the pure-logic unit suites are VERIFIED_TEST. Live token-exchange HTTP flows against real providers were not exercised (no credentials, per audit rules).

findings.title: Engine report list/download is not organization-scoped (cross-tenant exposure)
findings.description: The reports routes authenticate the session via sessionPrincipal(organizationId) but pass NO organization identifier to the engine. engineClient() is a single global EngineClient built from one MARKTING_ENGINE_URL + MARKTING_ENGINE_TOKEN; listReports() hits GET /reports and fetchReportFile(name) hits GET /reports/files/{name} with only the shared bearer token. organizationId is used only to prove the caller is logged into some org, never to filter which reports return.
findings.recommendation: Scope /reports and /reports/files/* to the caller's organization (run/thread ownership keyed on organizationId), or run one engine per organization and assert it in config/tests. Until then treat reports as a cross-tenant leak. If the shared engine does not isolate reports, this is effectively P0.

findings.title: MCP OAuth access/refresh tokens survive member deprovisioning
findings.description: authenticateMcpOAuthAccessToken and exchangeMcpRefreshToken validate revocation/expiry/claim-consistency but never re-check organization_memberships. OAuth tokens are tied to a user_id (sub). sessionPrincipal re-checks membership every call, but the token path does not. removeOrganizationMember has no path that revokes that user's mcp_oauth tokens.
findings.recommendation: Join organization_memberships in authenticateMcpOAuthAccessToken/exchangeMcpRefreshToken and revoke the user's access+refresh tokens inside removeOrganizationMember/changeOrganizationMemberRole.

findings.title: Production CSP permits script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'
findings.description: Outside development the CSP emits script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' (tests only assert unsafe-eval is excluded), permitting inline script execution site-wide; no nonce/hash CSP. Weakens XSS defense-in-depth. Current exploitability low: no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, React auto-escapes, report bodies streamed as attachment with nosniff.
findings.recommendation: Adopt nonce-based CSP via Next middleware and remove 'unsafe-inline' from script-src.

findings.title: Internal error messages returned to clients via forced 403
findings.description: apiError only masks the message and logs when status>=500. Several routes catch everything and force status 403, so an unexpected DB/runtime error is returned with the raw error.message and is never logged. Low-sensitivity internal detail (postgres constraint/column text) can leak, and genuine 500s are swallowed.
findings.recommendation: Derive status from the error via errorStatus; reserve forced-403 for real authorization failures; always log unexpected errors.

findings.title: No HSTS (Strict-Transport-Security) header set by the application
findings.description: The header block sets X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options, Permissions-Policy, COOP and CSP but no Strict-Transport-Security; grep for strict-transport/hsts found nothing. App relies on the hosting edge to enforce HTTPS.
findings.recommendation: Add Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload to the /(.*) header block.

findings.title: Cookie-authenticated JSON API routes have no explicit CSRF defense
findings.description: Dashboard mutation JSON routes authenticate purely from the Supabase session cookie and perform no Origin/Referer check or CSRF token. Server actions are covered by Next's built-in same-origin check and waitlist adds an Origin allowlist; these JSON routes do not. Protection rests implicitly on SameSite=Lax plus application/json CORS preflight. If the cookie became SameSite=None or a route added permissive CORS, they would become CSRF-able.
findings.recommendation: Add a shared Origin/Referer allowlist (as waitlist does) to state-changing JSON handlers.

findings.title: Member directory readable by any workspace member including viewers

findings.title: Direct-adapter (X Ads / OpenAI Ads) and model API keys omitted from redaction secret list
findings.description: _secret_values() enumerates only pipeboard/approval-signing/slack/database_url/api_tokens. The x_ads_* and openai_ads_api_key SecretStr values (live credentials used by direct adapters) are never added, and runtime.extra_secrets defaults to () and is never assigned in src. RedactionMiddleware therefore relies on regex alone for these opaque tokens; a raw X-Ads token echoed standalone in an upstream error would not be scrubbed before reaching the model/Slack/logs.
findings.recommendation: Add all *_ads_* SecretStr values (and model-provider API keys) to _secret_values or populate extra_secrets from them; value-based scrubbing is the only reliable path for opaque tokens.

findings.title: No key rotation / key-version support in cloud vault despite key_version column
findings.description: crypto uses a single ADPORT_CLOUD_ENCRYPTION_KEY with a format-version ('v1') but no key id; repository.ts hardcodes key_version=1. There is no keyring or re-encrypt path, so rotating the encryption key (or the API-key pepper) renders all stored provider credentials undecryptable and all API keys unverifiable.
findings.recommendation: Embed a key id in the ciphertext envelope, keep a primary+decrypt-only keyring in crypto.ts, add a re-encrypt job, and version the API-key pepper the same way.

findings.title: ADPORT_CLOUD_ENCRYPTION_KEY env validation weaker than real 32-byte requirement

findings.title: Engine report list/download routes have no tenant scoping (cross-tenant IDOR on a single shared engine)
findings.description: The engine is one shared process with a single report index and single out/ directory (one MARKTING_ENGINE_URL, one token mapped to caller 'adport-bridge', one shared engine-workspace volume). The two reports routes only call sessionPrincipal (any authenticated user of any org) and never scope the engine call to the caller's org. GET /api/reports/engine returns the whole shared index (run ids, windows, timestamps, summaries); GET /api/reports/engine/{name} streams any report file by name. A busy org also evicts other orgs' report-run history via the global 50-entry cap in _save_index.

findings.title: Write path cannot be driven by model output or injected text (core safety property)
findings.description: The markting bridge calls registry.call WITHOUT pending_operation_id, producing a preview only; the live write is a separate apply call gated by tools:write scope + owner/admin role + org-scoped lookup + non-self-approval. The engine's execute_change is wrapped in a LangGraph approve/reject interrupt and backed by a WriteGate (kill switch, writes-enabled flag, pinned catalog revision, canary allowlist) and two-person signed approval. Hostile-proposal tests confirm injection-driven proposals never reach a tool.
findings.recommendation: None; preserve these invariants under refactor. This is the central safety property and it holds.

findings.title: Read/write classification trusts provider-supplied readOnlyHint (deepest trust anchor)
findings.description: Tool READ classification reads annotations.readOnlyHint directly from Pipeboard MCP metadata. A compromised/buggy provider could mislabel a mutating tool (named to evade the mutate|raw|delete|remove|purge deny patterns, e.g. campaign_update/budget_set) as readOnlyHint=true; it would then be model-callable via PipeboardReadProvider.call_read and execute an un-governed side effect with no proposal, approval, or WriteGate. Contingent on compromise of the trusted MCP backbone, but it is the single deepest trust assumption and bypasses the entire write-governance stack.
findings.recommendation: Corroborate readOnlyHint with a host-side explicit read-tool name allowlist (mirroring admitted_mutations); alarm when a refresh flips a tool's hint/class; prefer an allowlist over trusting the annotation.

findings.title: Stripe events applied with no ordering/version guard; stale state can re-grant entitlements
findings.description: applySubscription writes plan/status/period straight from event.data.object and re-runs maxActiveAccounts enforcement. processStripeEvent dispatches on event type only. Nothing compares event.created, a subscription version, or re-fetches the live subscription, and billing_events stores no ordering key. Since each distinct event passes the by-id dedup, Stripe's unordered delivery lets an older customer.subscription.updated (active) arriving after customer.subscription.deleted (canceled) reactivate a paid plan and re-enable ad accounts.
findings.recommendation: Re-fetch the authoritative subscription via stripe.subscriptions.retrieve(id) before writing, or persist and compare a per-subscription monotonic high-water mark (event.created) and drop stale writes; add an out-of-order regression test.

findings.title: Idempotency check not atomic with processing (TOCTOU on concurrent re-delivery)
findings.description: Dedup SELECT, applySubscription, and the billing_events INSERT are three separate db() calls, not one transaction. Two concurrent deliveries of the same event.id can both pass the dedup, both run applySubscription (duplicate audit_events row + redundant account-disable scan), then the second INSERT is a no-op via on conflict. DB updates are idempotent so state damage is limited, but duplicates are processed rather than rejected. The one existing test never delivers an event twice, so this path is untested.
findings.recommendation: Claim the event first inside the processing transaction (insert ... on conflict do nothing returning 1; skip if no row) and run applySubscription in that same transaction so the claim rolls back on failure.

findings.title: Authenticated support endpoint has no rate limit (email amplification / cost)

findings.title: No RLS-enforced tenant isolation on the server (adport_backend) path
findings.description: Every table grants adport_backend a blanket 'using(true) with check(true)' policy and no table has FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. For the role that runs all server queries, RLS is an unconditional allow; cross-tenant safety relies entirely on each query carrying 'where organization_id = principal.organizationId'. All current queries scope correctly and resolveMembership validates the org against membership, so there is no current leak, but the DB offers no backstop.
findings.recommendation: Adopt session-GUC RLS for the backend role (set local app.org + policies on organization_id = current_setting), or add a CI guard rejecting org-keyed queries lacking an organization_id predicate; enable FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.
findings.failure_scenario: A future server query over an org-keyed table (e.g. a new report/list helper) is written without 'where organization_id = ...'; because adport_backend policies are using(true), it returns or mutates rows for every tenant with no policy to stop it -> cross-tenant disclosure.

findings.title: Server-path isolation silently depends on connecting as a non-owner role
findings.description: RLS binds only because adport_backend is not a table owner/superuser and no table uses FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. The connection sets role via the postgres.js startup GUC (default adport_backend). If SUPABASE_DB_URL logs in as owner/superuser and that GUC is dropped or ignored, the session bypasses RLS entirely, disabling even the browser-facing authenticated deny policies.
findings.recommendation: Add a startup/health assertion that the session role is adport_backend with rolbypassrls=false; enable FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. Runtime login identity NOT_VERIFIED (needs a live connection).
findings.failure_scenario: A deploy sets SUPABASE_DB_URL to the owner/postgres role and the role GUC fails to apply; every policy is bypassed at once and PostgREST/authenticated and server paths lose all tenant scoping, with no test detecting it.

findings.title: Inconsistent RLS enablement across private.* tables
findings.description: private.provider_credentials, private.oauth_transactions, private.rate_limit_buckets, the private.mcp_oauth_* tables and private.billing_events have no 'enable row level security', while provider_account_selections, synthetic_reviewer_workspaces and cloud_waitlist do. The unprotected ones (including the credential and OAuth-token tables) rely solely on schema/table grant revocations, which are sufficient because the private schema is not PostgREST-exposed and authenticated/anon have usage revoked, but the layered defense is uneven for the most sensitive tables.
findings.recommendation: Enable default-deny RLS uniformly on every private table so the most sensitive tables are not protected by grants alone. Deployed PostgREST exposed-schema list NOT_VERIFIED (schema revoke makes it moot).
findings.failure_scenario: A future migration adds a table to the private schema and grants it to authenticated for one feature without RLS; because the private-schema tables set no RLS precedent, the table is exposed with no policy backstop.

findings.title: Demo seed connects as Postgres superuser and service-role key

It is explicitly a local demo tool and all its SQL is parameterized tagged templates, so it has no injection risk; the only risk is operational if an operator points it at production credentials.
findings.recommendation: Keep it out of all deploy workflows and optionally assert the target DB host is loopback before executing. Operational GAP, not a code defect.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator exports production SUPABASE_DB_URL and SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY into the .env the script reads and runs it; it writes seed/demo rows into the production project with full privilege, bypassing RLS.

findings.title: Pending-operation apply is not atomic: concurrent double-apply (replay) to ad platforms
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/repository.ts:81 (contrasting OAuth consume uses for update + consumed check)
findings.description: PostgresPendingStore.get is a plain select (no FOR UPDATE) and delete sets consumed_at=now() with no 'and consumed_at is null' guard, and the route's find->apply->consume is not transactional. Two concurrent POST /api/approvals/{id}/apply both pass get() and both call provider.applyWrite before either consumes. policy-engine.test.ts:94-105 only proves sequential replay is blocked; there is no concurrency guard or test.
findings.recommendation: Consume via compare-and-set: update ... set consumed_at=now() where id=... and consumed_at is null returning id, inside db().begin with select ... for update, BEFORE applyWrite; 0 rows => PENDING_ALREADY_CONSUMED. Mirror the existing OAuth-transaction pattern. Add a parallel-apply test asserting exactly one platform write.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin double-clicks Apply (or client retries) on a 'create campaign' pending op; two requests race, both read consumed_at=null, both execute applyWrite -> two live campaigns created with real spend.

findings.title: Engine report surface has no tenant scoping (cross-tenant visibility of report runs/files)
findings.description: The single shared engine host stores report runs in one out/markting-reports.json with no organizationId; /reports and /reports/files/{name} are gated only by one shared bearer token. The cloud GET /api/reports/engine returns the full global list and streams any file by name, so every tenant sees all tenants' report runs and can download their files. Real impact bounded today because assert_fail_closed forces PAID_MEDIA_DATA_MODE=sample (synthetic data, shared label); becomes P0 if the engine ever carries real per-tenant data.
findings.recommendation: Partition report runs/files by organizationId end-to-end, or document the engine report surface as global sample-only that must never carry tenant data.
findings.failure_scenario: Tenant A calls GET /api/reports/engine, receives tenant B's run ids/summaries/file names, then GET /api/reports/engine/{B-file} downloads B's report.

findings.title: Budget-delta and absolute budget caps are not re-checked at apply
findings.description: apply() re-runs only checkStaticPolicy (protected accounts); checkBudgetPolicy runs only in validate(). A pending op validated under looser caps can be applied after an owner tightens max_daily_budget_micros/max_budget_delta_pct, up to the TTL window. The engine.ts:110 comment ('Policy may have changed ... re-check') overstates what is re-checked.
findings.recommendation: Re-run checkBudgetPolicy in apply() against current policy using the stored preview.budgetDeltas, or re-preview and compare before executing.
findings.failure_scenario: User previews a budget raise allowed at 25%; owner lowers the delta cap to 10%; within 15 min the pending op is approved and the >10% raise is applied without re-check.

findings.title: Preview shown to approver can be stale relative to applied effect
findings.description: apply executes a fresh provider.applyWrite(op) and returns the stored pending.preview without reconciling actual vs previewed. The op hash covers inputs only; preview fromMicros/summary reflect validate-time account state. Target value stays deterministic so this is a trust/clarity defect, not value divergence.
findings.recommendation: Re-preview at apply and show/compare, or annotate preview with validated-at and fail if fromMicros drifted beyond tolerance.
findings.failure_scenario: Account budget changes after preview; approver sees stale 'from X% -> Y%' delta that no longer matches reality at apply time.

findings.title: Completed write with no audit entry if audit append fails after applyWrite
findings.description: apply order is applyWrite -> audit.append('applied') -> pending.delete, with no pre-write intent record. If the audit DB insert fails after the external write succeeds, the write exists with no 'applied' audit row and the un-consumed pending remains applicable (compounds E10-01). Invariant #13 fails under audit-store failure.
findings.recommendation: Write an 'applying' intent audit row before applyWrite and/or consume the pending in the same transaction as the audit append; reconcile intent vs applied asynchronously.
findings.failure_scenario: applyWrite sets a budget; audit_events insert then throws (constraint/outage); platform shows the change but audit log has no applied entry and the pending can be re-applied.

findings.title: Null created_by silently disables the self-approval guard
findings.description: The four-eyes check short-circuits when row.createdBy is null (API-key- or engine-created pendings store created_by=null), so any owner/admin may apply them. Org-scoped, not cross-tenant, but separation-of-duties silently does not apply to that class.
findings.recommendation: Record a stable actor identity for API-key/engine-created pendings and define approval policy for them explicitly instead of relying on a null short-circuit.
findings.failure_scenario: A pending op created via an API key (created_by null) is approved by the same human who holds that key, bypassing maker/checker.

findings.title: Dashboard apply cannot reach a valid pending op beyond the 200 most recent
findings.description: apply/reject fetch a capped ordered list (limit 200/50) and .find by id rather than fetching the row by id; with many live pendings an older valid op 404s. Availability/correctness edge, not a security bypass.
findings.recommendation: Fetch the pending row by id directly, scoped by organization_id.
findings.failure_scenario: Org accumulates >200 live pending ops; applying an older but still-valid op returns 404.

findings.title: Pending-operation apply is not atomic: concurrent double-apply to ad platforms
findings.description: PostgresPendingStore.get has no FOR UPDATE; delete sets consumed_at=now() WITHOUT 'and consumed_at is null'; apply is get->applyWrite->audit->delete outside any transaction. Two parallel POST /approvals/{id}/apply both pass the null-consumed read and both call provider.applyWrite -> duplicated real-platform writes (double budget change, duplicate campaign). Invariant 12 BROKEN. The sibling OAuth consume at repository.ts:81-104 uses the correct for-update+consumed_at pattern.

findings.title: Stripe subscription events applied with no ordering/version guard
findings.description: applySubscription writes plan/status/period straight from event.data.object; processStripeEvent dispatches on event type only; billing_events stores no event created timestamp or subscription version. Stripe does not guarantee delivery order, so an out-of-order customer.subscription.updated(active) after deleted(canceled) reactivates a paid plan and re-enables ad accounts (active plan governs maxActiveAccounts = spend ceiling).
findings.recommendation: Re-fetch the authoritative subscription via stripe.subscriptions.retrieve(id) before writing, or persist and compare event.created plus a per-subscription high-water mark and drop stale writes. Add duplicate and out-of-order regression tests.

findings.title: No admin/owner revocation of MCP OAuth grants; grants also survive member deprovisioning
findings.description: The only revoke path requires the client's own token (RFC 7009); there is no authenticated admin/dashboard revoke. Token auth never re-checks organization_memberships, and removeOrganizationMember does not revoke the user's mcp_oauth_* tokens. Access tokens live 1h, refresh 30d. Merges E2-01 (P1) + E1-02 (P2).
findings.recommendation: Add an owner/admin 'disconnect this app' endpoint that server-side-revokes all tokens for a (client_id,user_id,resource) grant; revoke a user's mcp_oauth_* tokens on removal/role change; join organization_memberships in authenticateMcpOAuthAccessToken/exchangeMcpRefreshToken. P1 because an MCP client can spend ad budget for up to 30 days with no tenant-side kill switch.

findings.title: Budget caps not re-checked at apply (financial guardrail bypass window)
findings.description: apply() re-runs only checkStaticPolicy (protected accounts); checkBudgetPolicy (max_budget_delta_pct, max_daily_budget_micros) runs only in validate(). A pending op validated under looser rails applies after the rails are tightened, up to the per-op TTL (default 15 min). Invariant 5 PARTIAL. The inline comment 'Policy may have changed ... re-check' overstates the re-check.

findings.title: Completed real write can have no audit record if audit append fails
findings.description: Order is applyWrite (external side effect) -> audit.append('applied') -> pending.delete, with no pre-write 'applying' intent row. If the audit insert throws after the platform write, the write exists with no applied record and the un-consumed pending stays applicable (enables a duplicate, compounding SEC-02). Invariant 13 PARTIAL.
findings.recommendation: Write an 'applying' intent audit row before applyWrite and consume the pending in the same transaction as the audit append; reconcile intent vs applied asynchronously and alert on orphans.

findings.title: Engine /proposals/{id}/reject and /edit perform no caller/ownership authorization
findings.description: get_proposal enforces requester_ref/approver_refs visibility; reject and edit resolve 'who' but pass it straight to runner.reject/runner.edit, which only check proposal existence/state. Any holder of a valid engine bearer can reject or rewrite proposal field values by UUID regardless of ownership. Mitigated in the markting product (single adport-bridge caller + EngineClient FORBIDDEN_PATHS block /edit and /approve). P1 in any multi-token engine deployment or if the shared token leaks.
findings.recommendation: In runner.reject/runner.edit require who == record.changeset.requester_ref or who in approver_refs, matching get_proposal.

findings.title: Provider-supplied readOnlyHint is the sole trust anchor for read/write classification
findings.description: Engine catalog classification reads annotations.get('readOnlyHint') from Pipeboard MCP tool metadata. A mutating tool mislabeled readOnlyHint=true, with a name that evades the mutate|raw|delete|remove|purge deny patterns, is admitted as a model-callable READ with no proposal, no approval, no WriteGate -> complete bypass of write governance. Contingent on the trusted Pipeboard backbone being compromised/buggy; the single deepest trust assumption in the design.
findings.recommendation: Treat readOnlyHint as a hint, not authority: maintain an explicit host-side read-tool allowlist (names) so a tool must be named to be callable; alarm when a catalog refresh flips a tool's hint/class.

findings.title: Direct-adapter (X Ads, OpenAI Ads) and model-provider API keys omitted from engine redaction
findings.description: _secret_values enumerates only 7 secrets (pipeboard token, approval signing key, 3 slack secrets, database_url, api tokens). X Ads consumer/OAuth keys, openai_ads_api_key and model-provider keys (ANTHROPIC/GROQ) are absent; extra_secrets defaults to () and is never assigned. The value-based scrubber is the only reliable pass for opaque tokens, so a raw token echoed standalone in an upstream error body/stack reaches the model, Slack and logs unredacted.
findings.recommendation: Drive redaction from the full SecretStr registry (populate extra_secrets from all *_ads_* and model-provider SecretStr values) so new credentials scrub automatically.

findings.title: MCP refresh-token rotation lacks reuse detection and revocation cascade
findings.description: A consumed refresh token used after the 60s grace is merely rejected, never triggering family revocation (RFC 9700 4.14.2). Revoking an access token does not revoke the refresh token and vice-versa (RFC 7009 2.1). Refresh-token theft before legitimate rotation yields a fresh valid pair with no detection; after an explicit revoke, derived access tokens stay valid to expiry.
findings.recommendation: On presentation of a consumed refresh token outside the grace window, revoke all refresh+access tokens for that (client_id,user_id,resource) and log a security event; cascade revocation across access/refresh siblings.

findings.title: Web security headers weak: CSP 'unsafe-inline' and no HSTS
findings.description: Production CSP keeps script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' (no XSS backstop) and sets no Strict-Transport-Security. No injection sink exists today (React auto-escapes; no dangerouslySetInnerHTML - grep exit 1), so defense-in-depth only for a product that executes ad-budget changes.
findings.recommendation: Move to nonce-based CSP dropping 'unsafe-inline'; add Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload.

findings.title: No CSRF token on cookie-authenticated state-changing routes or OAuth consent
findings.description: Dashboard mutation JSON routes and the OAuth consent POST authenticate purely from the Supabase session cookie with no Origin/Referer check or CSRF token. Protection rests on SameSite=Lax (not pinned in code) plus CORS preflight. If the cookie is ever SameSite=None, or a route adds permissive CORS, these become CSRF-able; combined with open DCR an attacker could mint an auth code to a logged-in victim.
findings.recommendation: Add a shared Origin/Referer allowlist (as waitlist already has) to state-changing JSON handlers, a per-session signed CSRF token on the consent form, and pin the Supabase cookie sameSite explicitly.

findings.title: Preview shown to approver can be stale relative to the applied effect
findings.description: apply executes a fresh provider.applyWrite but returns the stored validate-time preview with no post-apply reconciliation; from->to and percentage reflect account state at validate time. Target value stays deterministic (hash-locked), so the material change is bounded - a trust/clarity defect, not value divergence. Invariant 4 PARTIAL.
findings.recommendation: Re-preview at apply and show/compare, or annotate the preview with 'as of <validated-at>' and fail if fromMicros drifted beyond a tolerance.

findings.title: No DB-level per-tenant RLS; isolation rests entirely on application WHERE clauses
findings.description: The adport_backend role (every server query) has *_backend_all using(true) with check(true) and there is no force row level security, so the DB gives no tenant backstop - one missing org predicate is a cross-tenant breach. Posture also silently depends on the runtime logging in as the non-owner role. private.* RLS enablement is inconsistent (provider_credentials and the OAuth-token tables rely on grants alone). Merges E4-03/E7-01/E7-02/E7-03. I found no current query missing its org predicate.
findings.recommendation: Add per-org RLS keyed on a request-scoped GUC (set_config('app.current_org',...)) plus organization_id = current_setting(...)::uuid policies; enable force row level security; add a CI lint rejecting org-keyed queries without an organization_id predicate; enable uniform default-deny RLS on every private table.

findings.title: Engine has no tenant concept; all threads/proposals/reports share one caller_ref
findings.description: The engine's own ownership/visibility checks are a no-op across tenants because every org maps to the single adport-bridge caller. Isolation is pushed entirely to the cloud (thread-id namespacing). Any future route forwarding a user-controlled thread_id/proposal_id to the engine without the cloud prefix/ownership gate yields trivial cross-tenant reads; reports already lack such a gate (SEC-01).
findings.recommendation: Issue one engine token per organization so the engine's own ownership checks become real defense-in-depth behind the cloud gate; never treat the engine as a tenant boundary.

findings.title: Platform read/write scope rests on a trusted readOnly boolean, no central path allowlist
findings.description: requireScope keys on definition.annotations.readOnly end to end; registry.call does not enforce scope. Passthrough *_api_read tools accept method:POST + arbitrary path and are safe only because each provider re-validates against a read allowlist (verified apple/microsoft/reddit). A future passthrough read tool without an allowlist, or a write tool mis-annotated readOnly:true, would silently grant read-only keys write capability.
findings.recommendation: Enforce read/write classification centrally (a registry invariant that readOnly passthrough tools must declare a method/path allowlist) and add a conformance test asserting POST-capable read tools reject a known mutation path.

findings.title: Provider text enters the model instruction zone (indirect prompt injection)
findings.description: Pipeboard tool descriptions are injected verbatim into the model's tool list, and read payloads/entity names flow back to the model. Classic indirect-injection carriers. Blast radius bounded: the model can only call account-scoped reads and propose_change (human-gated), raw rows are offloaded to artifacts, and UI rendering is escaped.
findings.recommendation: Sanitize or host-author provider-supplied tool descriptions keyed by tool name; tag/delimit provider-origin strings so the model treats them as untrusted data; strip control sequences in previews.

findings.title: Model-written report HTML served from the app origin without a sandbox CSP
findings.description: Report HTML is restricted to html/pdf/json, forced Content-Disposition attachment, nosniff, private no-store, and the name is validated against path traversal; but the response carries no sandbox / default-src 'none' CSP of its own and relies on the attachment disposition. A client/extension rendering it inline would execute model-written markup in a file/blob context.
findings.recommendation: Add Content-Security-Policy: sandbox (or default-src 'none') to the report response and/or serve it from an isolated origin.

findings.title: Internal/engine error detail leaked to clients
findings.description: apiError masks the message only for status >= 500; several routes catch everything and force 403, returning the raw error.message without logging (console.error is gated on >=500). Engine error detail up to 300 chars is passed through to dashboard users. Not a credential leak but exposes internal error shapes and swallows genuine 500s.
findings.recommendation: Let apiError derive status from the error and reserve forced-403 for actual authorization failures; always log unexpected errors; return a generic message for engine-origin errors and log the detail server-side.

findings.title: Stripe idempotency check is not atomic with processing (TOCTOU)
findings.description: processStripeEvent does SELECT dedup, then applySubscription, then INSERT ... on conflict do nothing as three separate db() calls. Concurrent re-delivery of the same event.id can both observe no row and both run applySubscription (updates are idempotent, but an audit_events row is inserted each pass and the account-disable scan re-runs). Compounds SEC-03 if a stale duplicate wins the race.
findings.recommendation: Claim the event first inside the processing transaction (insert ... on conflict do nothing returning 1; skip if no row) and run applySubscription in the same transaction.

findings.title: Authenticated support endpoint has no rate limit; honeypot signals rejection
findings.description: Unlike waitlist, the support route performs no throttling; each POST triggers an outbound transactional email. A single authenticated tenant user can flood the support inbox and run up email cost. The honeypot raises a ZodError -> 400, signalling rejection to a bot rather than returning a success-shaped response.
findings.recommendation: Add enforceRateLimit('support:org:<orgId>') plus a global bucket; make the honeypot path return {ok:true}.

findings.title: Null created_by disables self-approval guard; apply limited to 200 most-recent pendings
findings.description: The four-eyes check is 'if (row.createdBy && row.createdBy === principal.userId && ...)', so it short-circuits for API-key- and engine-created pendings (created_by null) - any owner/admin may apply them (still org-scoped, so not cross-tenant). Separately, apply/reject fetch listPendingOperations(org,200).find(id) instead of fetching by id, so an older valid op beyond 200 returns 404.
findings.recommendation: Record a stable actor identity for API-key/engine pendings and define approval policy explicitly; fetch the pending row by id scoped by org rather than via a capped list.

findings.title: Encryption-key rotation impossible despite key_version column; weak env key check
findings.description: crypto uses a single ADPORT_CLOUD_ENCRYPTION_KEY with no key-id envelope or keyring; key_version is hardcoded 1; rotating the key or the API-key pepper would make every stored credential undecryptable/unverifiable with no re-encrypt path. The env schema accepts any >=40-char string while crypto requires exactly 32 decoded bytes, so a misconfigured key fails lazily at first OAuth connect rather than at boot.
findings.recommendation: Embed a key id in the ciphertext envelope, keep a primary+decrypt-only keyring, provide a re-encrypt job, version the pepper, and validate base64-decodes-to-32-bytes in the zod schema.

findings.title: Supply-chain pinning gaps (actions, supabase CLI, docker images, infra lockfile)
findings.description: GitHub Actions are referenced by mutable tags (only one SHA-pinned), including release.yml which holds NPM_TOKEN and id-token; make up fetches and runs supabase@latest unpinned with --yes; Docker base images are tag-only (no digests); infra/ has no lockfile and installs with npm install --no-audit next to Stripe credentials.
findings.recommendation: SHA-pin every uses: with a version comment; pin supabase to an exact version or add it as a dev dependency; pin FROM ...@sha256:<digest>; commit infra/package-lock.json (or fold infra into the pnpm workspace), pin stripe, and drop --no-audit. Enable Dependabot github-actions + docker at root.

key_findings: The write boundary is the system's strongest property: only PolicyEngine (engine.ts:113) reaches a real applyWrite, the engine host is proposal-only/kill-switched/sample-pinned, and no model output or injected provider text can execute a write without human approval - invariants 1-3 HOLD (VERIFIED_CODE + VERIFIED_TEST).

Of the 15 invariants: 9 HOLD, 5 PARTIAL, 1 BROKEN. The BROKEN one is replay (SEC-02): pending-op apply has no for-update/compare-and-set, so two parallel approvals both execute a real ad-platform write.

Tenant isolation is enforced entirely by application WHERE clauses (no DB RLS backstop for the server role); it holds everywhere I could trace EXCEPT the engine reports surface (SEC-01), which has zero org scoping in production route code - P1 today (synthetic data), latent P0 on real data.
Two financial-integrity gaps beyond writes: Stripe events apply with no ordering guard (SEC-03, can reactivate a canceled paid plan) and budget caps are not re-checked at apply (SEC-07).
Supply chain is the weakest systemic area: Next.js 16.3.1 has 3 critical RCE advisories (SEC-04, VERIFIED_RUNTIME) and no CI/secret/dependency gate runs on the shipped monorepo root (SEC-05).

MCP OAuth containment is incomplete: no admin kill switch for a rogue grant, grants survive member deprovisioning, no refresh-reuse detection or revocation cascade (SEC-06, SEC-14) - serious because an MCP client can spend ad budget.

22/22 spot-checked specialist citations were confirmed against code; no specialist inflated severity. The only judgement I overrode was the reports IDOR, raised from E4/E10's P2-today to a consolidated P1 (latent-P0), with reasons.
E11.disagreements: Resolved against code: (1) Engine reports IDOR severity - E1-01/E5-01 rated P1, E4-01/E10-02 rated P2-today/latent-P0. I confirmed the /reports endpoints exist only in services/engine-demo/serve_demo.py (production engine app.py has no /reports route) and docker-compose runs that host pinned to sample data with one adport-bridge token, so today only run metadata + synthetic fixtures cross tenants. Resolved to P1 (latent-P0): the defect is in production route code carrying zero org scoping, not in the demo pin; P0 is reserved for when real tenant data actually crosses. (2) MCP grant lifecycle - merged E2-01 (P1, no admin revoke) with E1-02 (P2, survives deprovisioning) into SEC-06 at P1 given the budget-spend blast radius and 30-day window. Doc-vs-code contradictions the specialists surfaced and I re-verified: engine.ts:110 comment 'Policy may have changed ... re-check' overstates the re-check (only static policy, not budget - SEC-07); translate.ts claim 'prose never chooses the tool/account/target' holds for tool+account but target_ref passes through for live accounts lacking a targets map; README/PHASE reports frame tenant isolation as living in markting_threads but never extend that to the reports surface, which has no org dimension; migration headers imply RLS-enforced isolation but the backend role has using(true) with no org scoping (app-level only).
E11.not_verified: No live/runtime exploitation of the app was attempted (no Postgres/Supabase in the sandbox; DB-integration and concurrency tests not executed) - all app findings are VERIFIED_CODE, only the supply-chain audit is VERIFIED_RUNTIME. Deployment/runtime facts that move severities and remain NOT_VERIFIED: whether production is ever multi-org on one engine and whether a real-data report host gets wired to the unscoped routes (SEC-01 P1 vs P0); the runtime Supabase cookie SameSite value (SEC-16); the runtime DB login identity vs adport_backend and whether the role GUC is applied (SEC-18); reachability of Next.js image-optimization/next/og routes (SEC-04 P1 vs P0); currency/budget units for 7 of 11 providers (invariant 10 spot-checked on google/meta/tiktok/snapchat only); and whether the hosting GitHub repo adds a root .github not present in this checkout (SEC-05). I spot-checked 22 citations but did not re-verify every citation in all ten E reports.

D11.scope: Synthesis of D0–D10 subsystem reports into a system architecture map (docs/audit/04-system-architecture-map.md) with component/request-flow/ER/deployment Mermaid diagrams; 15-citation spot-check; inter-agent disagreement reconciliation; consolidated deduplicated findings with final severities.

git log --oneline | tail -5 => 0 (import commits fa7bf19/4162146 confirmed)

findings.title: Apply of a pending operation is not atomic: concurrent or retried apply executes the provider write twice
evidence: platform/packages/core/src/policy/engine.ts:88-124 (get → applyWrite → audit.append → delete, no atomic claim)
platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/repository.ts delete = unconditional `update … set consumed_at = now()` (no `consumed_at is null`, no returning)
D7 runtime probe S1: applyWrite calls = 2; S2: re-appliable after post-write audit failure
findings.description: Consolidates D4-01/D5-01/D7-01/D7-02/D7-03/D9-01/D1-06/D2-08. The two-step contract guarantees hash/expiry/policy but not exactly-once execution; the irreversible provider write precedes any durable marker, across three non-transactional writes spanning two systems. Two admins/tabs, an MCP retry, or a crash between applyWrite and delete all cause a second execution. The engine already has the correct pattern (pma_approvals conditional UPDATE WHERE used_at IS NULL).
findings.recommendation: Add a claim primitive to PendingOperationStore: `update pending_operations set consumed_at = now() where id = $1 and organization_id = $2 and consumed_at is null and expires_at > now() returning *`, call it before applyWrite, record a `failed` outcome on provider error, and add a packages/core concurrency test. Terminal state column (applied|rejected|expired|failed) instead of bare consumed_at.

findings.title: Engine can never read connected accounts; 'live' is a real model over fixtures, yet proposals can route to real ad accounts via alias bindings
evidence: services/engine-demo/serve_demo.py:163-166 (assert_fail_closed refuses non-sample), :183-191 (demo_settings forces sample), :383-388 (live branch coerces to sample)
platform/apps/cloud/lib/markting/repository.ts:40-50 + translate.ts:133-142 (an alias may bind demo-google to a real provider/account)
README.md:83,116 claims 'Analyses connected accounts' and DEMO_MODE=false = real accounts
findings.description: Consolidates D0-01/D10-01 (+ D8 observation). Every engine mode reads only google_ads/meta_ads/reddit_ads.json; OAuth-connected adport accounts are never visible to the engine. The product's central promise is DOCUMENTED_NOT_IMPLEMENTED (capability MOCK_ONLY). In live mode the Assistant's synthetic analysis can be translated into a guarded write on a real account bound to a demo-* alias; only the policy cap and the human apply stand between fiction and a real budget change (UNSAFE_TO_AUTOMATE).
findings.recommendation: State plainly in README/TODO that the engine is fixture-only. Before any live rollout feed the engine real reads (adport-backed read provider or Pipeboard with data_mode=live), or make the bridge refuse to bind non-sandbox providers while /health.catalog_source=='fixture'.

findings.title: Engine report surface is global/cross-tenant (list, download, run); /markting/info unauthenticated; one global lock
evidence: services/engine-demo/serve_demo.py:324-374 (one index file, one asyncio.Lock, token-only checks, no org dimension; info() has no caller())
serve_demo.py:163-166 forces sample so leaked content is synthetic today
findings.description: Consolidates D1-01/D4-03/D8-01/D8-06/D8-07/D10-08/D3-07/D7-07/D9-04. No tenant dimension at any layer: every org lists/downloads/triggers every other org's runs; a global asyncio.Lock serialises all tenants' renders (noisy-neighbour DoS); WeasyPrint renders synchronously on the event loop (D9 measured a 1.36 s stall). ESCALATES TO P0 the moment assert_fail_closed is relaxed. Agent divergence (D1/D8 P1, D4/D7/D10 P2, D3 P3) reconciled to P2-today/P0-if-real.
findings.recommendation: Pass an org key to /reports/run, index per org under out/<org>/, filter listing/download by org, record an adport audit event per run; move render off the event loop (asyncio.to_thread); authenticate /markting/info; per-org quota + bounded queue.

findings.title: One engine identity for all tenants: engine-side ownership/visibility checks are tautological; isolation is a single cloud-side thread-id convention
findings.description: Consolidates D8-02/D7-08/D5-05. The engine is tenant-blind; ThreadAccessDenied can never fire between tenants and every proposal is visible to the single bridge token. All conversation isolation rests on the org_<org>__u_<user>__ thread-id format being generated and checked correctly in one place. Any holder of MARKTING_ENGINE_TOKEN or any future route that forwards a client thread/proposal id has full cross-tenant access.
findings.recommendation: One engine token per organization (the engine already supports token:caller pairs) or an X-Organization-Id header the host namespaces thread ownership, proposal visibility and reports by; add two-caller engine tests and a platform test rejecting a foreign thread id.

findings.title: Demo scripted model shares per-process mutable state across threads; the second conversation gets 'script exhausted', concurrent turns corrupt each other
evidence: services/engine-demo/serve_demo.py:84-115 (seen_human_messages/call_count/steps are instance fields; reset keyed on human-message COUNT, not thread id; one instance per process)
D3/D7/D10 probes: thread B's first message returns the exhausted text; concurrent threads interleave scripts
findings.description: Consolidates D3-01/D7-04/D10-02. In the shipped default mode the Assistant works only for the first conversation after boot and strictly alternating message counts; a second user/tab breaks it. Invisible to make test because each test builds a fresh app. Demo-only (no safety impact) but demo is the default and only exercised mode.
findings.recommendation: Key script progress by config['configurable']['thread_id'] (available in RunnableConfig) or build one model per thread; guard with a lock; add two-thread sequential and asyncio.gather tests.

findings.title: Chat turn is a single synchronous HTTP call held open for minutes: no job, no streaming, no idempotency key, no cancellation
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/app/api/assistant/messages/route.ts:7 (maxDuration=300, a no-op on the Node standalone server)
platform/apps/cloud/lib/markting/engine-client.ts default 240s abort, single fetch, no retry; health() unused
engine MessageIn is only text (no idempotency key); graph.ainvoke has no server deadline
assistant-chat.tsx browser fetch has no AbortController
findings.description: Consolidates D1-02/D7-05/D9-02. A live-model turn blocks one browser connection for minutes behind any proxy/LB (most terminate at 60-120s). Client abort does not cancel the engine graph (INFERRED); the natural retry runs the turn twice; a page reload loses the conversation (threadId only in React state).
findings.recommendation: Make the turn a job: route returns 202 + turn id; a worker calls the engine with an idempotency key (the engine's DedupeStore exists) and a server-side timeout; persist messages per thread; UI polls/SSE; surface threadId in the URL for resume; fast-fail on /health.

findings.title: Stale awaiting_approval proposals are re-bridged on later turns; unsupported proposals never handed back; failed hand-off swallowed → duplicate pending rows and overwritten provenance
evidence: bridge.ts:58-66 (unsupported branch returns with no handoff), :98-105 (handoff catch {} silent)
repository.ts:84-86 (on conflict … do update set pending_operation_id = excluded — earlier id lost)
engine runner.py:134 returns the latest thread proposal regardless of turn
D7/D9/D10 probes: next turn returns the same awaiting proposal
findings.description: Consolidates D1-03/D7-11/D7-12/D9-03/D10-03/D10-04/D10-09. The dual-write between the engine DB and Supabase has no saga state. Any hand-off failure/timeout/unsupported path makes every later message re-translate the stale proposal, creating a second applyable pending row for one human request and orphaning the first from provenance. D1-03: registry.get(tool) runs OUTSIDE the try/catch, so an UNKNOWN_TOOL (alias bound to an unconnected provider) dangles the proposal with a raw 404 and no record. D10-04: the assistant route has no tools:write check, so a reader-plan user triggers a proposal, loses the reply and is 403'd on every later turn of that thread.
findings.recommendation: Bridge only proposals created in this turn (require interrupted===true or compare proposal_id/created_at); check tools:write before calling the engine; always hand unsupported/refused proposals back to the engine; persist hand-off as a retried step with its own status; move registry.get inside the guarded block; never swallow rejectOnEngine failures.

findings.title: No per-thread serialization on either side: concurrent messages run two graph invocations on one checkpoint
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/markting/repository.ts:17-27 (claimThread is an upsert, not a lease)
engine surfaces/runner.py:86-89,208-213 (ownership check only; no Lock/Semaphore)
D7/D9 probes: two concurrent change requests → divergent outcomes, lost HITL interrupt
findings.description: Consolidates D7-06/D9-10. The UI busy flag is the only serialisation. Two tabs, a retry, or a future API client interleave checkpoint writes; with the Postgres checkpointer and a real model the interleaving is undefined and the interrupt can be lost while the proposal stays awaiting_approval.
findings.recommendation: Per-thread lease in the cloud (pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(thread_id)) or a markting_thread_locks row) returning 409 when a turn is in flight; an asyncio.Lock per thread id in the host (or a DB lease for multi-process).

findings.title: Organization deletion destroys its own audit trail, never writes deletion_requests, is non-transactional, and revokes only the Google token
evidence: D5 scratch run T2: audit_after_org_delete = 0; rg finds no writer of deletion_requests
findings.description: D5-02. The deletion_requested audit event is cascaded away milliseconds after it is written, leaving no erasure record. deletion_requests (with its enum, indexes, RLS, retention rule) is never written. Non-Google provider tokens stay valid on the provider side; a partial failure leaves a half-deleted tenant.
findings.recommendation: Record lifecycle events outside the org cascade (nullable org_id or a copy); use deletion_requests; wrap the DB part in one transaction; revoke every provider's tokens; fan out to the engine (see C12).

findings.title: Three auth.users foreign keys have no ON DELETE action (and are NOT NULL): a user who created an org/connection/API key can never be deleted
evidence: migrations/20260817171039_cloud_initial_schema.sql:28 organizations.created_by, :61 connections.connected_by, :118 api_keys.created_by — each `uuid not null references auth.users(id)` with no action
D5 scratch T7: delete from auth.users → FK violation
findings.description: Consolidates D5-03/D6-06. GDPR/erasure requests fail with an FK error; app/api/deletion/route.ts:25 deletes the user only when they have zero memberships and the FK still blocks. created_by/connected_by are provenance columns that should not pin user rows.
findings.recommendation: Recreate the FKs as `on delete set null` and make the columns nullable (as pending_operations.created_by already is), or record actors in profiles; add a regression test deleting a creator who is no longer a member.

findings.title: Assistant threads become claimable by any org member once their owner's auth user is deleted
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/markting/repository.ts:22-23 (claimThread accepts user_id is null), :33 (listThreads returns null rows to everyone)
D5 scratch T7b: after deleting a member, her thread shows user_id=NULL and is visible to another member
findings.description: Consolidates D5-05/D8-05/D6-11. Same-tenant disclosure of private conversation content (the thread content lives in the engine checkpoints under the same thread_id). Divergence reconciled (D5 P2, D8 P3) to P2 on D5's runtime evidence; D8 rated P3 only because the current single caller adds a prefix check that claimThread itself does not enforce.
findings.recommendation: on delete cascade for markting_threads.user_id (and delete the engine checkpoint thread), or treat user_id is null as 'nobody'; move the prefix check into the repository.

findings.title: No retention/purge for markting_*, MCP OAuth, waitlist, or engine pma_*/checkpoints; tenant deletion never reaches the engine
evidence: engine persistence/postgres.py:11-43 (no tenant column, no purge; LangGraph checkpoints keyed by thread_id only)
findings.description: Consolidates D5-04/D6-07/D8-04/D9-08. A tenant's full conversation history, proposals and receipts persist indefinitely in the engine database after the org is deleted; MCP tokens and Slack dedupe keys grow unbounded; the per-tenant data_retention_days promise is silently incomplete for the markting feature (the most sensitive content).
findings.recommendation: Extend apply_data_retention to markting_threads/markting_engine_proposals/markting_sandbox_state; schedule purge_expired_mcp_oauth_records; add an org-scoped engine purge endpoint called from deletion and retention (delete thread_id like 'org_<org>__%' and checkpoints); add a test asserting every table is in the retention function or an allow-list.

findings.title: organization_settings.policy and data_retention_days are writable directly via PostgREST by owner/admin, bypassing plan cap, validation and audit
evidence: server path enforces cap+audit+policySchema only in lib/cloud/tenant-admin.ts:167-195 via app/api/settings/route.ts
browser can reach PostgREST: next.config.ts connect-src includes the supabase origin; public schema exposed (config.toml:14)
findings.description: D6-01. An authenticated owner/admin can PATCH organization_settings for their own org with any body, skipping the plan's maxRetentionDays (free plan=30, CHECK allows 3650), the settings_updated audit event, and policySchema validation. A malformed policy breaks every subsequent getOrganizationPolicy (self-DoS); a permissive policy (require_validation:false, cap null) is set with no audit trail — for a product whose safety story is policy+approval+audit. Not cross-tenant (requires membership).
findings.recommendation: Drop the browser UPDATE policy/grant (keep select); if a browser write path is wanted, expose a security-definer RPC that enforces the cap, validates the JSON and writes audit; add `check (jsonb_typeof(policy)='object')`.

findings.title: Backend connects as the DB owner (postgres) with a per-connection SET ROLE; the adport_backend least-privilege boundary is advisory
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/db.ts:13 (connection: { role: ADPORT_DB_ROLE }) — a wire-level SET ROLE after login, not a separate login
adport_backend is nologin noinherit granted to postgres (migration:4-11); no LOGIN role inherits it
default strings are the owner (.env.example:8, docker-compose.yml:25); no code checks current_user after connect
findings.description: D6-02. What is deployed is the database owner with a per-connection SET ROLE. Any statement that RESET ROLE regains owner privileges (private + auth schemas); a transaction-mode pooler that drops the startup `role` parameter would silently run as postgres (BYPASSRLS in Supabase, INFERRED) with nothing noticing. The boundary is one statement thick and rests on 'the app never runs raw SQL'.
findings.recommendation: Create adport_app (LOGIN, in role adport_backend, ALTER ROLE … SET role = adport_backend for pooler safety), connect as it, and add a startup self-check (select current_user must equal ADPORT_DB_ROLE else refuse to serve); keep the owner out of SUPABASE_DB_URL.

findings.title: Monthly report deterministically fails on the demo fixture, but the Reports page exposes the button
evidence: D9 probe: POST /reports/run {cadence:monthly} → 500 ComputeError (previous window needs 56 days, fixture read returns 28)
host test covers weekly only (test_demo_api.py); engine-reports.tsx:54 offers 'Run monthly'
findings.description: D9-05. In demo mode the monthly button can never succeed; because failed runs are not persisted (C3) nothing but a transient toast records it.
findings.recommendation: Hide/disable monthly in demo mode or widen the fixture read window; add a monthly host test; persist failed runs as report.run.failed.

findings.title: Stripe webhook idempotency is check-then-act outside the state transaction; no ordering guard; processing errors returned as 400
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/billing.ts:120-136 (select billing_events then applySubscription then insert on conflict do nothing, outside the transaction)
webhook/route.ts:12-15 returns 400 for any processing error (same as bad signature)
findings.description: Consolidates D9-06/D5-10. Unmodified upstream adport code. Concurrent deliveries of one event both pass the existence check and double-process; a late older event overwrites newer plan state; a transient DB failure is reported to Stripe as 400, indistinguishable from signature tampering. Sequential replays are protected. D9 argued P2 (plan regression/flap); kept P3 as upstream + concurrency-dependent.
findings.recommendation: Insert the event id first in the same transaction as the state change (no row → duplicate); store event.created and skip older-than-last per subscription; return 2xx fast and process from an outbox; 5xx (not 400) for processing failures.

findings.title: Refresh-token rotation is performed inline during reads; a persistence failure loses a rotated refresh token
evidence: packages/snapchat/src/client.ts:145-148 (sets this.refreshToken then awaits onRefreshToken; Pinterest/Spotify identical)
runtime is created per request so the in-memory token does not survive
findings.description: D9-07. Unmodified upstream code; the CAS logic itself is correct (credential-rotation.test.ts passes). For providers that rotate the refresh token on every refresh, the old token is already invalid when the callback runs; if the DB write fails for any reason other than 'grant changed' (pool exhaustion, lock timeout, deploy) the new token exists only in a discarded request-scoped object and the connection is dead until re-authorization.
findings.recommendation: Persist first with bounded retry (same CAS); emit credential.rotated/rotation_failed events; consider a dedicated near-expiry rotation job instead of rotating inside reads.

findings.title: DELETE /api/members is unreachable from the Team page: the client sends a JSON body, the route reads query parameters
evidence: docs/TODO.md:37 / PHASE0-REPORT.md:89 list it as known and unfixed
findings.description: D4-02. With no query string z.string().uuid().parse(null) throws and apiError(error,403) returns 403 with a Zod blob. The shipped 'Remove member' feature always fails with an opaque 403.
findings.recommendation: Accept the body on DELETE (or switch the client to query params); add a route test.

findings.title: Session-route error contract is unreliable: auth/membership failures become 500 or 403, raw Zod/Postgres messages leak, wrong status classes
evidence: lib/cloud/auth.ts:12 throw new Error('Authentication required.') string-matched in six routes
apiError(error,403) in 11 routes maps every failure (Zod, auth, provider, Postgres) to 403 with verbatim error.message (lib/http.ts:24-33)

resolveMembership throws a plain Error → 500 in the markting routes; /mcp maps any non-HttpError to 401 (mcp/route.ts:65); /oauth/[provider]/start → 401 for everything; dashboard/summary → 400 for everything
findings.description: Consolidates D4-06/D4-07/D1-08/D2-05. Clients cannot distinguish 'fix your input' from 'not allowed' from 'retry later'; internal DB messages reach browsers; 5xx monitoring is polluted by user errors; one edit of the auth string silently turns 401s into 500s.
findings.recommendation: One pipeline: ZodError→400 with issues, auth→401, membership/role→403, HttpError as-is, AdportError per the map, else 500 with a request id and no message; validate path/body ids with Zod before touching the DB; only HttpError(401) should emit the /mcp WWW-Authenticate challenge.

findings.title: Four-eyes (requester != approver) is enforced only on the dashboard route; REST and MCP apply with no such check and API-key rows have created_by null
evidence: app/api/v1/tools/[tool]/route.ts and app/mcp/route.ts only check scope; authenticateApiKey returns a principal with no userId/role
