key_findings: Two P1 defects cut across the whole system: (C1) apply has no atomic claim, so a concurrent or retried approval executes the real ad-platform write twice — reproduced at runtime by D7; and (C2) the engine can never read connected accounts (fixture-only in every mode) yet synthetic-data proposals can be routed to real accounts via alias bindings.

Cross-tenant isolation is a single-layer convention: the engine is tenant-blind (one caller_ref for all orgs, C4), its report surface is global (C3, P2 today / P0 if data mode is relaxed), and the Postgres backend role bypasses RLS (using(true), C24) so a forgotten WHERE clause is an immediate leak.

The engine host is a single-process, single-replica, unscalable SPOF: shared scripted-model state breaks the 2nd conversation (C5), one global lock serialises all tenants' reports and blocks the event loop, and the monthly report always fails on the fixture (C15).

Chat and approvals are synchronous dual-writes with no job/queue/outbox (C6, C7, G2): turns are minutes-long HTTP calls with no idempotency, stale proposals get re-bridged, hand-off failures are swallowed, and the apply/preview path writes to two databases with no transaction.

Tenant lifecycle is broken: org deletion destroys its own audit trail and never reaches the engine (C9, C12), three auth.users FKs block user deletion (C10), and deleted users' private threads become claimable by other members (C11).

D5 is the only agent that executed the Postgres paths (scratch cluster, 4/4 bridge DB tests, behavioural probes T1-T9), so it is authoritative for database behaviour and upgrades several findings from VERIFIED_CODE to VERIFIED_RUNTIME.

The single-write-path safety invariant is genuinely sound and fail-closed (ProposalOnlyWriteProvider + kill switch + no approvers + assert_fail_closed + EngineClient refusing approve/edit), and apply replays the re-validated, re-hashed stored payload — the safety architecture holds even though the operational one does not.

All 15 spot-checked citations reproduced exactly at HEAD 41b069e; the eleven reports are mutually consistent and independently corroborate the five cross-cutting defects, with divergences only on severity calibration (reconciled in the map's §13).
D11.disagreements: Inter-agent disagreements were all about severity calibration or about what each agent could execute, never matters of fact. (1) Double-apply: D4/D5/D7/D9 rated P1, D1-06 rated P2 ('upstream weakness') — reconciled to P1 on D7's runtime reproduction and the 26 non-idempotent create tools. (2) Engine global reports: D1/D8 P1, D4/D7/D10 P2, D3 P3 — reconciled to P2-today (synthetic content; real exposure is metadata + shared-lock DoS) explicitly escalating to P0 if assert_fail_closed is relaxed. (3) Thread-claim-after-delete: D5 P2 (ran T7b showing the null-then-claimable path), D8 P3 — reconciled to P2 on D5's runtime evidence. (4) Stripe webhook: D9 P2, D5 P3 — kept P3 (unmodified upstream, concurrency-dependent) noting D9's argument. (5) Demo/self-approval flags: D1/D6 P2, D0/D8/D10 P3 — reconciled to P2 because MARKTING_ALLOW_SELF_APPROVAL is independent of demo mode and removes four-eyes on real accounts. Methodological divergence: most agents left the Postgres-backed paths NOT_VERIFIED (ECONNREFUSED), while D5 stood up a scratch cluster and ran them — D5 is treated as authoritative for DB behaviour. Doc-vs-code contradictions the agents found and I confirmed: README claims the engine 'analyses connected accounts' and DEMO_MODE=false=real accounts (contradicted by the forced sample mode); ARCHITECTURE.md:228 says there is no apply control (contradicted by the shipped apply routes); docs say 'scheduled reports' (nothing schedules); PHASE0/1 claim 'requires tools:write' on the assistant route and an unseen-(proposal_id,revision) pre-check (neither exists); migration comment says 'three fixture aliases' (four exist); '8 migrations' (nine); '177 passed' upstream (19 fail on the stray KILL_SWITCH in this tree).
D11.not_verified: D11 did not (and the whole team could not) verify: any container build or end-to-end make up/make seed run (Docker/network blocked for every agent); MARKTING_ENGINE_MODE=live with a real model key; production Supabase configuration (sign-up policy, confirmations, pooler mode, postgres BYPASSRLS, default privileges — config.toml governs the local CLI stack only); PDF rendering inside the engine image. The C1 double-apply is VERIFIED_RUNTIME against an in-memory store (D7 probes) and VERIFIED_CODE against the Postgres store, but not reproduced end-to-end against a live ad provider (none exists in the sandbox, by rule). The engine Postgres paths are VERIFIED_RUNTIME only through D5's scratch cluster, not the shipped compose stack. The 15-citation spot-check confirmed every cited structure at HEAD 41b069e; the reports' own line numbers occasionally drift by a few lines because the tree advanced during the parallel audit run.
